# Reproduction

The manifest embeds the exact probe sources, scripts and generated probe lockfile. Write each `reproduction` value under `artifacts/lean-ownership/` and the shared `probe_lock.content` to both probe destinations after generating their manifests. Arrays in `raw_micro_observations` are nanoseconds indexed by zero-based repetition; the summary scripts contain the paired bootstrap algorithm and seeds.

1. Check out baseline `23ec7c87a55c6c53043b5fc59befda627b08c560`; archive it into `artifacts/lean-ownership/baseline/` and `artifacts/lean-ownership/local-source/`. Apply `retained_patch` to the main checkout. Preserve the baseline tree. Reconstruct exploratory variants with `experimental_patches` only for the earlier exploratory campaign.
2. `build-screen-local.py` constructs control, routing-only, H2-only and retained-bundle variants at the same source path. It invokes `make-final-probe.py`; the generated probe lock must match the manifest before builds. Use Rust 1.96.0 for the recorded ARM64 setup. Run `screen-local.py` with no concurrent compilation or analysis, then `summarize-screen.py arm64-screen2`.
3. For Linux, create the provided temporary pod on a suitable disposable host (adapt node selection, namespace and CPU masks). Copy the baseline checkout to `/work`, the embedded tools to `/work/artifacts/lean-ownership`, and make `/work/results`. Install Python, binutils and OpenSSL for the temporary harness. Use Rust 1.96.1. `build-screen-remote.py` overlays each variant at `/work` and preserves its binaries. Keep the probe lock identical for all builds. The original context name is `homelab`; adapt it to the measurement host.
4. Build `/work/results/pin` with `rustc -O /work/artifacts/lean-ownership/pin.rs -o /work/results/pin` and the k6 launcher with `rustc -O -C target-feature=+crt-static /work/artifacts/lean-ownership/pin.rs -o /work/results/pin-static`. Check CPU topology; the recorded masks select server CPU 2 and client CPUs 4 and 6. Run `screen-remote.py` in the server container, retrieve its CSV, then run `summarize-screen.py linux-screen2`. Stop all probe work before socket measurements.
5. Create a disposable localhost certificate with OpenSSL, including `subjectAltName=DNS:localhost`; put it at `/work/cert.pem`, key at `/work/key.pem`, and allow the client to read the certificate. The script trusts it with `SSL_CERT_FILE`, without disabling TLS verification. Copy `load.js`, `client-loop.sh` and `remote-load.py` to `/work`. Confirm no server listener or stale job/result files. Start `client-loop.sh` in the client container and `remote-load.py` in the server container; redirect each to a log and retain each exit code. The controller owns and waits on server processes. It refuses existing result keys. The final script smoke-tests all eight workloads, then measures seven. The completed plaintext pairs came from the preceding controller, using the same binaries and workload settings; include plaintext in the measured steps for a fresh full campaign.
6. The first 256-VU attempt exceeded the original fixture's 117-connection admission. `server-bounded.rs` changes only the benchmark request-body bound to 1 KiB; `admission.rs` verifies 117 before and 1,409 after using the actual core API plus the TCP TLS I/O adjustment. `build-bounded-remote.py` expects the baseline/candidate source files in `/work/bounded-input/control` and `selected2`, and `server-bounded.rs` alongside them. It rebuilds both at `/work`, preserves separately named binaries and records identities. After both builds succeed and all prior server/client jobs stop, launch a fresh client loop and `remote-bounded.py`. Its four 256-iteration preflights must pass before the fixed two-workload, ten-pair campaign. Client CPU statistics require cgroup v2 `cpu.stat`. Keep this configuration separate from all earlier results.
7. `preflight.py`, `large-routes.py` and `sse-isolated.py` perform separate validation/size checks. Do not run them concurrently with timed probes on the same host. Keep failed attempts separate. Download results, then delete the temporary namespace. Never commit generated certificates, binaries, build trees or raw console logs.

This is an experimental reproduction bundle, not supported product tooling. A different CPU, compiler, allocator, runtime backend, body ownership pattern or offered load can change results. The trial CSV and manifest preserve the observations used for this PR; they do not establish performance on every workload.
